Hi Camila / Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier — the demo helped a lot. We pulled together a couple of quick questions so we can scope the pilot:  

1) Auth & SDK: can you confirm what SDK flows you recommend for server-side integration? We need short-lived credentials and a service-account style approach for our indexing pipeline. Do you support fine-grained key scopes (read-only embeddings vs scoring)?

2) Routing / fallbacks: our product will have a latency requirement of ~120ms P95 for the search page. If the primary reranker is busy, can requests automatically fall back to a lighter model (embedding-similarity or a smaller ranker)? How are fallbacks configured per route?

3) Evaluation & metrics: attached is a small set of testcases (rerank-testcases.csv) — we want guidance on which metrics to run (MRR vs nDCG@5/10, pairwise loss) and recommended sample sizes. Also curious about recommended top_k and whether you typically tune top_k differently per use-case.

4) Structured output/tool calling: we plan to call out to a post-processing service that annotates results with category tags. Any best practices for structured outputs from a reranker (JSON schema expectations, tokenization quirks we should watch)?

If helpful, Marcus from ops (cc) can share our current auth model. Would you be able to run a quick sanity evaluation against the attached CSV and share sample run output + next steps for a tech workshop?

Thanks,
Emily

Hi Emily — great questions, thanks for sending the CSV. High level answers up front, then a proposed plan & next steps.

Short answers:
- SDK/Auth: we recommend our server-side SDK with service account keys + short-lived JWTs minted via your KMS. Yes — we support scoped API keys (embeddings-only, generate-only, score-only).
- Routing/fallbacks: yes — route policies can be configured per API route. You can set a primary reranker and fallback chain (e.g., small ranker -> embedding similarity). Fallbacks can be triggered by latency, error rate, or capacity.
- Metrics & top_k: we typically run nDCG@5 and MRR for reranker pilots and examine nDCG@1/5/10. Start with top_k=10 for the candidate generator and tune the reranker top_k (we often score at top_k=50 internally but return top_k=10 to the UI).
- Structured output: return a compact JSON payload per candidate (id, score, normalized_score, tags:[], metadata:{}) — avoid long text fields in the score call to reduce tokenization variance.

Proposed pilot:
1) Run our evaluation harness against your CSV (we'll produce run_results_sample.json). We'll measure nDCG@1/5/10, MRR, pairwise disagreement, and latency distribution.
2) Quick auth alignment: Ben will share the recommended key rotation flow and a short architecture diagram for the short-lived token minting.
3) Tech workshop / runbook: 60min technical workshop (deep dive on SDK, routing, caching, KV reuse).

Action items / owners:
- Redwood: run evaluation on attached CSV + share run_results_sample.json (Ben) — ETA: 48 hours.
- Searchly: confirm preferred workshop window next week and share any other evaluation slices to include (Lauren: can you confirm whether we should include geo/time slices?).
- Ops sync: confirm whether service account pattern is allowed on your side (Marcus).

I'll drop a shared doc and a rough timeline in the next email. Thoughts?

—Camila

Emily — quick technical notes (happy to expand during the workshop):

1) top_k & scoring: two-stage common pattern — candidate generation (embeddings ANN) at top_k_gen=500, reranker scoring at top_k_score=50 and final_cut=10. For latency-sensitive pages we push candidate gen to 200 and score 20.

2) Metrics: nDCG@5 and normalized MRR give different perspectives; also look at pairwise accuracy if you care about swap errors between near-equal candidates. For confidence, sample ~1k labeled queries across your traffic slices.

3) Batching & KV caching: for interactive UI, continuous batching helps but maintain small max_wait (5-12ms). Use KV caching for common prefixes — this cuts CPU for autoregressive rankers.

4) Auth scopes: use three scopes — embeddings.read, rerank.score, admin.* (rotate admin keys less frequently). We recommend Azure/GCP KMS/HSM for minting. I attached a simple auth-flow diagram for ops (will share auth-flow-diagram.png).

I can run the evaluation harness and produce a sample run by EOD tomorrow. Also, if you can tell us typical candidate set size (after your ANN filter) and P95 latency target for the page, I'll include tuned params in the report.

—Ben

- Labeled sample: we can easily provide ~1.2k labeled queries across product slices; attached is a tiny sample run JSON (run_results_sample.json) representing our internal format.
